dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these episodes usually happen during the night, and do you remember what happens in your dreams?

I usually have these bad dreams a few hours after I go to sleep, and they make me wake up feeling really scared. I can remember seeing scary things in my dreams, and that makes me not want to go to bed at night.
When you wake up, are you fully alert and able to talk to your parents, or do you feel confused and groggy? Also, have you been feeling extra stressed or worried about anything during the day lately?

I'm usually wide awake when my parents come in, and I can tell them all about the scary things I saw. I don't feel stressed during the day; everything at school and with my friends is normal and happy.

Do your parents notice if you move around a lot or scream while you are still asleep, or do you mostly stay still until you wake up? Also, do you drink any sodas or eat snacks with caffeine in the evening?

My parents say I yell and cry quite a bit when it's happening, but I always remember exactly why I was so scared once I'm awake. I don't drink soda or eat caffeine in the evening because my mom says it's not good for me before bed. I mostly just stay in my bed, but I'm really tired the next day at school.
Do your parents ever notice you snoring loudly or having trouble breathing while you are asleep? Also, has anyone else in your family ever had trouble with bad dreams or sleep problems?
My mom and dad say I breathe normally and don't make any loud snoring noises when I'm sleeping. No one else in my family really has bad dreams like I do, so it's just me who gets scared at night.

Are you currently taking any medications or vitamins, and do you notice your heart racing or that you are sweating when you wake up from these dreams? I would also like to know if these episodes happen every

I don't take any medicines or vitamins, but my heart does beat really fast and I feel all sweaty when I wake up from the scary dreams. These episodes happen about once or twice a week, usually a few hours after I first fall asleep.

How long has this been happening, and have you noticed any other changes in your health, like headaches or feeling weak? I am going to request a sleep study to observe your sleep patterns more closely
It has been happening for about two months now, and I haven't had any headaches or felt weak at all. I’m just really tired the next day because it's hard to go back to sleep after such a scary dream.

RESULTS: Not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination.

Based on your description of remembering the vivid, scary details and being fully alert when you wake up, it sounds like you are experiencing nightmares rather than night terrors. Since this is affecting

I'm glad you think so, because being scared in the dark is the worst part. Is there something we can do so I don't have to be afraid to go to sleep anymore? I just want to stop feeling so tired when I'm at school with my friends.

We can certainly help you get back to having restful nights by establishing a relaxing bedtime routine and discussing some comforting techniques for when you wake up. Based on everything you have told me, your symptoms

I really hope those things work because I hate seeing the scary things in my head when I close my eyes. Will I have to keep waking up and feeling my heart beat fast like that? I just want to feel normal and not be the only one in my class who is always so sleepy.

With the right steps, we can definitely help those scary dreams go away so you feel rested at school. Since you remember the dreams clearly and wake up fully alert, everything points to a specific condition.

That makes me feel much better because I don't like being frightened and waking up all sweaty. Do you think I'll be able to stop procrastinating at bedtime once the dreams go away? I just want to wake up feeling like I have enough energy to play with my friends.
Yes, once you feel safe and know that your dreams will be peaceful, you'll find it much easier to go to bed on time. I have all the information I need to help you.

Thank you, Dr. Agent, I really hope I can start sleeping better soon. It will be so nice to go to school without feeling like I need a nap right away. I'm ready to try whatever routine you think will help me feel safe at night.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. 

It is wonderful that we have a plan to help you feel safe and rested again. Sleep well and things will get better soon!
